description.narrative: 2,370 participants (50% women, 50% men and 10% MmB) in Baquba actively apply community-based leadership approaches, dialogue formats and initiatives to build bridges for sustainable peace

Overall objective: By 2027 youth resilience and social cohesion is enhanced within conflict-affected communities in Baquba and Muqdadiya districts by combatting violent extremism.Project objectives: Participants are endowed with skills and resources to improve their livelihoods; trust between diverse ethnic and religious groups is fostered; women and youth are empowered to actively engage in decision-making processes at the households, district- and sub-district levels.

The direct target group includes individuals from Baquba district in Diyala Governorate, representing diverse ethnic and religious backgrounds, including persons with disabilities, government officials, and local authorities. The project focuses on promoting social cohesion, vocational and leadership training, and institutional capacity building. Young adults will receive technical and leadership training to enhance their role in community decision-making and lead initiatives that foster coexistence and mutual respect through social media, workshops, and local events. These efforts will create a ripple effect, empowering others and amplifying the project’s impact. The initiative supports youth-led projects outlined in the Diyala Action Plan and encourages collaboration with other successful initiatives and platforms to promote innovation and peer learning. Community and religious leaders, respected for their influence and ability to mobilize, will facilitate dialogue, mediate disputes, and promote reconciliation by focusing on shared goals. Local authorities will participate in workshops and leadership sessions, integrating knowledge into governance and using their networks to reduce tensions and build trust. The project will also connect authorities with youth and women’s groups to promote mentorship and knowledge exchange, strengthening social structures across communities. Additionally, ARD will engage water user associations, farmers’ groups, and irrigation committees to incorporate sustainable water management practices into broader efforts to enhance social cohesion.
